To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gravitational radiation from the pre-big bang scenario is a stochastic signal with a spectrum that is tilted towards high frequencies and that it is characterized by two parameters.

a spectrum of relic gravitational radiation, strongly peaked towards high frequencies, emerges in a class of superstring cosmological models, and that the required sensitivity for its detection is within reach of some of the planned gravitational-wave detectors.

a spectrum of relic gravitational radiation, strongly skewed towards high frequencies, characterized by two basic model parameters, and detectable by the proposed space interferometer LISA, emerges in a class of String Theory models.

the study of cosmology and gravitational radiation from the early universe in the context of string cosmology.
the study of the cosmological and astrophysical aspects of superstring theory, and in particular with the study of gravitational waves from the early Universe.

we have shown that string cosmology is a very promising candidate for the generation of gravitational radiation in the frequency range from 1 Hz up to 10 4 Hz.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a stochastic background of gravitational radiation is a generic prediction of string theory and that it is within reach of the planned gravitational-wave detectors.
string theory provides a concrete realization of the idea of inflationary cosmology and a natural framework for studying the origin and the evolution of our universe.
the stochastic relic radiation from string cosmology may be detected by future gravitational-wave detectors.
